# Philemon {.unnumbered}

##### Chapter 1

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="scripture" data-book="Philemon" data-chapter="1">
<p><span class="drop-cap">P</span>aul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer, <span class="verse-number">2</span> And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house: <span class="verse-number">3</span> Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. <span class="verse-number">4</span> I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers, <span class="verse-number">5</span> Hearing of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints; <span class="verse-number">6</span> That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus. <span class="verse-number">7</span> For we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother. <span class="verse-number">8</span> Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient, <span class="verse-number">9</span> Yet for love's sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ. <span class="verse-number">10</span> I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds: <span class="verse-number">11</span> Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me: <span class="verse-number">12</span> Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels: <span class="verse-number">13</span> Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel: <span class="verse-number">14</span> But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly. <span class="verse-number">15</span> For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever; <span class="verse-number">16</span> Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord? <span class="verse-number">17</span> If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself. <span class="verse-number">18</span> If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account; <span class="verse-number">19</span> I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides. <span class="verse-number">20</span> Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord. <span class="verse-number">21</span> Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say. <span class="verse-number">22</span> But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you. <span class="verse-number">23</span> There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus; <span class="verse-number">24</span> Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers. <span class="verse-number">25</span> The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.</p>
</div>
:::

\begin{scripture}[Philemon][1]
\lettrine[lines=4]{P}{aul,} a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer,
\vs{2}And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house:
\vs{3}Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
\vs{4}I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers,
\vs{5}Hearing of thy love and faith, which thou hast toward the Lord Jesus, and toward all saints;
\vs{6}That the communication of thy faith may become effectual by the acknowledging of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.
\vs{7}For we have great joy and consolation in thy love, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
\vs{8}Wherefore, though I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin thee that which is convenient,
\vs{9}Yet for love's sake I rather beseech thee, being such an one as Paul the aged, and now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
\vs{10}I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds:
\vs{11}Which in time past was to thee unprofitable, but now profitable to thee and to me:
\vs{12}Whom I have sent again: thou therefore receive him, that is, mine own bowels:
\vs{13}Whom I would have retained with me, that in thy stead he might have ministered unto me in the bonds of the gospel:
\vs{14}But without thy mind would I do nothing; that thy benefit should not be as it were of necessity, but willingly.
\vs{15}For perhaps he therefore departed for a season, that thou shouldest receive him for ever;
\vs{16}Not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved, specially to me, but how much more unto thee, both in the flesh, and in the Lord?
\vs{17}If thou count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.
\vs{18}If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account;
\vs{19}I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it: albeit I do not say to thee how thou owest unto me even thine own self besides.
\vs{20}Yea, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: refresh my bowels in the Lord.
\vs{21}Having confidence in thy obedience I wrote unto thee, knowing that thou wilt also do more than I say.
\vs{22}But withal prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.
\vs{23}There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus;
\vs{24}Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.
\vs{25}The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
\end{scripture}
:::
